PROCESS.description: Tuner peg hole position and spacing error in the headstock
Fret slot position error against nominal scale, causing intonation error that cannot be tuned out
String spacing at the nut uneven across the board
Truss rod channel off-centre or off-depth, giving uneven relief and thin walls
Heel geometry outside tolerance for the body pocket, giving a loose or forced joint
Fretboard radius inconsistent along the length of the board

SPECIFICATION.description: A body wood used as a neck wood, typically basswood or nato sold as mahogany
Janka below the threshold for hardware retention, so fret tangs, tuner bushings, screws and the truss rod anchor all bear on wood that crushes
Grain runout at the headstock transition, the standard break location
Blank not dried to service equilibrium, so the neck moves after the instrument is assembled
Soft single-action rod with rolled threads that strip under adjustment
Unbranded soft fretwire that wears into divots early in service

LABOUR.description: Frets not level to one another, giving buzz and dead notes
Crown profile flattened or uneven after levelling, blurring intonation at the contact point
Fret ends sharp or proud of the board edge
Nut slots cut high, giving stiff action and sharp intonation at the first frets
Orange peel, sags, witness lines or a finish left thick enough to deaden response

risk_profile.note: Latent and non-remediable together is the worst pair: the defect cannot be found at receipt and cannot be fixed once it appears. On a built instrument it returns as a warranty claim rather than as a rejected part.

comparisons.question: Measured against one yardstick, how does a neck built here compare with the observed purchase - on coverage, on what can be verified, and on cost?
comparisons.verdict: NOT COMPARABLE. 7 defect mode(s) cannot be closed by any spend: DEF-FRET-SLOT-POSITION, DEF-GRAIN-RUNOUT, DEF-MOISTURE-CONTENT, DEF-SPECIES-SUBSTITUTION, DEF-TRUSS-CHANNEL-CENTRING, DEF-TRUSS-ROD-GRADE, DEF-WOOD-HARDNESS. Cost parity is unpurchasable, so no remediation figure is reported.

findings.metric: acceptance criteria that can be run, build against buy
findings.interpretation: Held to ONE yardstick, the decisive difference is not score - it is what can be checked at all. A neck built here can be judged against 17 of 17 criteria; the purchased neck against 3. The other 14 describe stages that happened in another shop to another standard, and the evidence is under a glued fretboard. Those are not failures, they are blanks - and 7 of them are also irrecoverable, so they can neither be found on arrival nor fixed later. Buying is not only cheaper, it is 18% verifiable. That is the trade the cost model could not see.

findings.metric: non-remediable modes left open by the observed import
findings.interpretation: The comparison the make-or-buy model ran for three days is REFUSED here. The observed import leaves 7 modes open that no spend can close, so its $35 and the shop's $187.88 are prices on different products and the difference between them is not a saving. No remediation figure is reported, because reporting one would imply parity is purchasable.

findings.metric: loss on the same unrecoverable fault, caught early against late
findings.interpretation: One fault, DEF-TRUSS-CHANNEL-CENTRING, priced on both sides. Built here it is measured at M1 before the fretboard goes on and the loss is 48.93. Bought in, there is no M1 to inspect at, so it surfaces only when the neck will not set flat - by then it is 187.88 inside a finished instrument. Identical verdict, 3.8x the loss. Owning the early stages is worth money even when the fault rate is the same on both sides.

findings.metric: defect modes eliminated at zero marginal cost
findings.interpretation: 6 of 17 modes are removed by holding position, at no marginal cost at all - because the machine indexes every feature from one datum, not because anyone tried harder. This is quality an hourly rate cannot erode, and it includes the canonical complaint about bought necks.

findings.metric: labour minutes attributable to quality modes
findings.interpretation: 113.0 of the shop's minutes go to the 5 labour-eliminated modes, costing 54.14. Against the 191 labour minutes in the cost model that is the majority of the neck's labour content, and the import spends none of it. The labour gap is not inefficiency to be squeezed out - it is the product, and squeezing it out means building the other thing.

No threshold in this gate has been set by the owner and no neck has been built, so the shop's full coverage is INTENT and its 100 percent verifiability is an opportunity rather than a result - owning the stages means the checks CAN be run, not that they have been. Every figure is a draft engineering estimate. This taxonomy exists to be overturned by the first build sessions; until then its job is to stop cost comparisons between things that were never the same product.
